claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit! To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm inquiring about my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex**. 

Before I can assess eligibility, I need to understand your circumstances better. Let me start with some key questions:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 17 years old.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Are you responsible for maintaining Alex - that is, do you provide for their food, accommodation, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, settled resident, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm a resident here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand your residency status more clearly to assess eligibility properly.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? If neither, do you have any other form of visa or immigration permission to be in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for clarifying that.

**Have there been any periods where Alex has been in hospital or in care (such as local authority care) for more than 12 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't been in hospital or in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I have most of the information I need. Let me just confirm one more important detail:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training (such as school, college, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has started an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the eligibility criteria using the official government guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official government guidance I've reviewed, I need to clarify an important point about Alex's eligibility.

The guidance states: **"You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England."**

This is a critical rule for your situation. Before I make my final determination, I need to confirm:

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or in Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex's apprenticeship is in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make my determination.

Based on the official government guidance for Child Benefit eligibility, I can now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Outcome: You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

**Reason:** While you meet the general eligibility requirements (you're a British citizen, living in the UK, and responsible for Alex), the critical factor is that Alex has started an apprenticeship in England. The government's Child Benefit rules specifically state that eligibility stops when a child starts an apprenticeship in England, even though they would normally continue to receive it if they were in other forms of approved education or training.

If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's circumstances change (for example, if they leave the apprenticeship and return to full-time education), please contact the Child Benefit Office for further advice.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and has started an apprenticeship in England. According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you will stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England. Although children aged 16-19 can normally continue to receive Child Benefit while in approved education or training, apprenticeships in England are specifically excluded from this provision. Therefore, Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit.

This rule applies regardless of the other positive factors in your situation."
